extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers, program officers, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions of institutional facilities, equipment, IT and data-management services, clinical sites, and administrative support provided in support of an R01 renewal application. Documents what resources are available to carry out the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCSF Voice and Data Services (ITS/ENS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UCSF Information Technology Services (ITS) hosts a centralized email server and provides basic voice and data services in support of the campus community. Enterprise Network Services (ENS) supports academic, research and administrative activities across the UCSF campus network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core services include network planning and implementation, voice and data network maintenance, remote access to UCSF networks, and internet access; ITS handles planning, coordination, policy development, implementation of new systems, and day-to-day operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium Desktop Support Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium Desktop Support (held by Drs. Gandhi, Bacchetti, Benet, and Gerona at UCSF) includes all services provided by Basic Desktop Support with differentiators increasing scope, flexibility, quality, and responsiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for customers whose needs extend beyond Basic Desktop Support (e.g., extended hours, faster response, support for non-standard or out-of-warranty hardware, enhanced training, onsite support for presentations, developer workstation support). Standard productivity software (Microsoft Office, Adobe Acrobat Pro) included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours of Support (Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service Desk support is available 24/7/365; onsite field support is available M-F 7-6; after-hours support available through Service Desk; field staff on-call for remote support; after-hours onsite support available with prior arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides continuous Service Desk coverage and arranged after-hours onsite support for UCSF locations when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Times (ITS/Support goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For incident responses, the ITS goal is to assign and acknowledge ticket assignments from the Service Desk within 2 business hours of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts will be made to respond to urgent issues in less time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware support (Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium Desktop customers are encouraged to purchase Dell or Mac hardware per JACS standards; non-standard hardware supported with business justification; out-of-warranty systems and systems >5 years old can be supported by special arrangement. Loaner laptops and projectors available for reservation up to 2 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports legacy lab equipment running legacy software by arrangement; flexibility for non-standard hardware when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software support (Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support includes local installations of clinical applications and other applications that may be out of manufacturer support, accommodated by special arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows special arrangements to maintain software where upgrades are not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage & Data Backup (UCSF Premium/Clinical apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical applications: 10GB individual file storage for specific folders (aggregated by department); Unlimited UCSF Box storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines quota for clinical application file storage and availability of unlimited Box storage for UCSF users.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Training (UCSF Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: On-site training for application support including expertise in productivity software (Office, Acrobat, Endnote) is available by special arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides tailored on-site training for software used by research teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Management (Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes project management for relocation coordination for larger office/lab moves (>3 people): network connectivity planning, static IP requests, disconnect/reconnect of equipment, configuration/confirmation of connectivity at new location, and follow-up floor support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports relocation logistics and ensures connectivity and immediate post-move support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation Support (Premium Desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Onsite presentation support at UCSF facilities including projector connectivity, wireless access configuration, and presentation troubleshooting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides technical onsite assistance for presentations and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Rights (Desktop Support differentiator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative rights are listed as a differentiator under Premium Desktop Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates elevated user/admin privileges are part of premium service offerings (no further specifics provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Data Management Systems (MyResearch)
rubrics_metrics.description: UCSF Academic Research Services provides secure transfer, storage, and analysis of research data via a firewalled system called MyResearch, accessed through an encrypted portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MyResearch enables storage of large volumes of data and houses statistical applications (SAS, SPSS, Stata), Stat/Transfer, Atlas.TI, RedCap; supports secure centralized data analysis environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Qualtrics and licensed statistical software
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualtrics is available to UCSF researchers free of charge. Desktop licenses for SAS and SPSS (including AMOS) are available for a modest annual fee (~$250) through UCSF library Research Software Licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers have access to survey tools and common statistical software either free or at modest cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Washington (UW) research infrastructure overview
rubrics_metrics.description: UW provides extensive environment for training and research with access to libraries (7+ million volumes), campus network access, mainframe resources, technology transfer, human subjects review, and grant/contract services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights breadth of institutional support including interdisciplinary collaborations and high federal funding history relevant to research capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICRC offices and conferencing facilities (UW)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICRC offices located on NJB provide ~6,000 sq. ft. for investigators/staff; office and conference rooms wired with T-100 Ethernet and dual voice/data; secure Wi-Fi. Eleven conference rooms available with data/phone/projector connections; six with wall-mounted LCDs; four with Polycom videoconferencing; one fully-equipped distance-learning classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details per-room capabilities (projectors, monitors, videoconferencing, webcasting, webinar and lecture capture capability) supporting large-scale tele/remote education and meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-capacity videoconferencing infrastructure (UW)
rubrics_metrics.description: One videoconferencing suite with dedicated Polycom system, 80-port hub, wall-mounted camera configured for enhanced telepresence and two wall-mounted LCD monitors enabling connections from up to 80 H.323-compliant clients and voice-only participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables large multi-site videoconferences with telepresence; supports both video and voice-only participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for early-stage investigators (UW ICRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICRC conducts weekly work in progress meetings for early stage investigators, provides career enrichment workshops and seminars, facilitates peer groups, and offers administrative and mentoring support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically names mentoring/co-mentorship for a supported early-stage investigator in the subcontract.

rubrics_metrics.name: UW computing resources and services
rubrics_metrics.description: UW provides Ethernet access, databases (Current Index to Statistics, Medline, library catalog), Nebula Managed Desktop Services, UW Google Apps (email with >7GB, Calendar, Docs, Talk), and UW Learning and Scholarly Technologies (LST) workshops and online curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nebula Managed Desktop includes software delivery/installation, phone support, shared file server space, security (patching, anti-virus), drive mappings, printer installs, file restores, Outlook setup; LST offers free workshops and web-based tools for teaching, learning and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICRC secure file servers and access controls (UW)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICRC uses secure file servers managed by UW IT with remote/local access, daily backups, redundant off-site backup storage, password-protected directories when necessary, and restricted sections reserved for the data team with exclusive password-protected access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Server access membership is regularly reviewed; changes to server access must be approved; files in directories may be password-protected as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary in-house IT support (ICRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: In-house IT provides on-demand software support, hardware troubleshooting, general technical support, computing services research, smartphone and A/V support, travel readiness sessions and post-travel computer check-ups; IT support available 24 hours a day in conjunction with UW IT services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes remote backup, secure external hard drives and redundancy for travelling employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management vendor & closed-system DataFax (DF/Net Research)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICRC contracts with DF/Net Research to perform data management using DataFax, an off-the-shelf study/data management package that uses fax machines, bar codes and ICR to collect and monitor clinical study data; CRF images processed by ICR and stored in a proprietary database on DataFax server; images remain electronic within DataFax throughout the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DataFax is considered a closed system with centralized data management at DF/Net; supports data entry, data quality control, and study management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security, audit trail, and access controls (DF/Net / DataFax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Security is included at system, DataFax, and procedural levels to limit data access to authorized individuals. All transactions are fully recorded in a secure audit trail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-house data staff are given view-only access via iDataFax; changes to portal access must be approved before implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: iDataFax and DF/Net web portal access for in-house staff
rubrics_metrics.description: In-house data staff have view-only access to a study’s DataFax database via iDataFax to view CRFs, data, and queries; they can view/download study reports or CRFs for printing via DF/Net web portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is role-restricted and does not allow changing data; portal access changes require approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleconferencing capabilities and monitoring (ICRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICRC regularly hosts complex international conference calls using standard international long distance or third-party teleconferencing service; both options require secure pins; calls to African countries are actively monitored in-house to ensure stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A monitor and teleconferencing operator work to ensure participants join and stay on the call; a log of all calls is maintained and regularly reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Videoconference systems and Adobe Connect server (ICRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Videoconferences utilize Skype, Polycom or Adobe Connect; two of four conference rooms equipped with HD cameras and projectors; all four have webcams and LCD screens; a keypad-secured control room houses the Adobe Connect server which is operable via advanced remote control pad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All systems supported in-house for reliability and remote operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harborview Medical Center HIV Clinic (Madison Clinic) facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Madison Clinic is a primary care clinic for HIV-seropositive persons, single largest provider of AIDS care in King County, located in a 12,000 sq. ft. medical office with onsite services (inhalation therapy, IV treatments, chemotherapy), pharmacy, laboratory, and shared conference rooms. ~1,300 patients/year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinic serves diverse patient population; is a nationally recognized outpatient teaching site for trainees who follow their own patient panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Washington Virology Research Clinic (VRC) facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: VRC contains ~4,000 sq. ft., 5 clinical exam rooms, 8 offices, study coordinator suite, check-in area, waiting room, laboratory and secure storage for charts/medications/specimens; laboratory includes centrifuge, microscope, -20C and -70C freezers and refrigerator; full-time courier transports research samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ample locked cabinet space for records; IT, laboratory and courier services provided by Department of Laboratory Medicine/Virology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seattle-King County STD Clinic resources and research databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Health – Seattle & King County STD clinic occupies 9,200 sq. ft. with 24 exam/counseling rooms, operates 50 hours/week, served 12,346 visits in 2010; maintains a clinical database documenting demographic/clinical/epidemiologic/behavioral data on >250,000 clinical evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Databases (including partner services and surveillance) are available for research following PHSKC review and removal of patient identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIDS Clinical Trials Unit (ACTU) capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: ACTU is one of 50 national ACTG sites, enrolls ~100 participants per year into clinical trials and natural history studies; located in a 4,500 sq. ft. medical office suite with eight exam rooms, a pharmacy, a laboratory, waiting room and medical records room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides infrastructure and experience for clinical trials recruitment and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Colorado-Anschutz Medical Campus facilities overview
rubrics_metrics.description: UC-AMC in Aurora is a major medical campus with ~$400M sponsored research awards annually; Division of Infectious Diseases housed in Research Complex 2 (RC2) with 19,518 sq. ft. of laboratory and office space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes institutional strength and space allocation supporting investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Colorado Infectious Diseases Group Practice (IDGP) clinical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: IDGP is the largest HIV/primary care clinic in Colorado located on 7th floor of UCH Anschutz Outpatient Pavilion, provides care for ~1,750 patients (17% women), staffed by 23 medical providers across multiple specialties and includes on-site pharmacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinic supports multidisciplinary care and strong ties to Division research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC-AMC computers and nightly backups
rubrics_metrics.description: A completely networked computer system with hardware connections to the greater University of Colorado Denver system is available to personnel for email, scientific writing, molecular analysis and information access; UC-AMC servers are backed up every night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides standard networked computing environment and nightly backup assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Colorado administrative resources for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Division provides administrative support for HR issues, grant budget monitoring/reporting, regulatory compliance and NIH-deadline monitoring, assistance with grant submissions, telephone/fax/photocopying/IT support, and proactive research development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes administrative assistance with clinical protocol development and regulatory submissions (IRB, CTRC) as a Division core service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major equipment at UCSF Hair Analytical Laboratory (HAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: HAL has one Agilent LC 1260- AB Sciex 5500 Triple Quadrupole mass spectrometer (quantitative targeted analysis), an Agilent LC 1260-QTOF 6550 (non-targeted analysis), and a Bruker Scion TQ GC-MS/MS for volatile non-polar compounds, plus accessories (nitrogen generators, SPE manifolds, tissue homogenizer, rotavap, centrifuge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab maintains necessary accessories/instruments to support LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS analyses and sample preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bio-sample storage and tissue culture facilities (HAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory maintains two -80 freezers (12 ft3), a -20 freezer (10 ft3), three 3 ft3 freezers, two 3 ft3 refrigerators, and shares a fully equipped tissue culture room with laminar flow hoods with adjacent laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides capacity for cold storage and tissue culture work supporting molecular/biochemical analyses.
